directionLimit: Emotion tags adjust pace and pauses. This model does not provide native acted emotions.

party-1.caption: Six weeks. Five times the users. Tonight, take a moment. You built this.
party-1.speaker: kavya

party-2.caption: I saved you a drink. Though Omar has been staring at that spreadsheet all night.
party-2.speaker: dani

mismatch-1.caption: The stage says one hundred twenty thousand in weekly payouts. My ledger says four hundred ten thousand.
mismatch-1.speaker: omar

mismatch-2.caption: Before anyone calls this sustainable, help me explain the difference.
mismatch-2.speaker: omar

sample-1.caption: Ana refers Ben. Ben refers Ana back. What should that pair earn? Try it here.
sample-1.speaker: dani

role-1.caption: You own referrals at Gilt, a neighborhood marketplace. I'm Omar, your finance partner.
role-1.speaker: omar

role-2.caption: I'm Dani. I run growth. We celebrated signups before checking who stayed.
role-2.speaker: dani

role-3.caption: I'm Kavya, the CEO. We have twelve weeks of cash. Find the real growth worth keeping.
role-3.speaker: kavya

role-4.caption: Three evidence pulls tonight. Then set payouts, protect useful customers, and explain the change.
role-4.speaker: omar

reply-1.caption: The board wants a sentence from you. Can we keep this growth going?
reply-1.speaker: kavya

guide-evidence.caption: Pick three reports. Each costs one pull. Opened reports stay in your case file.
guide-evidence.speaker: omar

guide-lens.caption: Try devices, purchases, and location. Separate fake accounts from people who really buy here.
guide-lens.speaker: dani

guide-valve.caption: These controls change weekly payouts. Watch runway, then commit a week to see the result.
guide-valve.speaker: omar

week-1.caption: The signup curve moved. I need to know which customers we lost, not just how many.
week-1.speaker: dani

week-2.caption: Exactly. Cheaper growth means little if we cut the customers who create value.
week-2.speaker: omar

message-1.caption: People are asking if mutual referrals are a feature. What can we honestly promise tonight?
message-1.speaker: kavya

call-1.caption: I'm Tomas. I work with the neighborhood Guilds. Those gold loops are actual shops.
call-1.speaker: tomas

call-2.caption: Leena's bakery sends customers to the florist. They send people back. Both make sales.
call-2.speaker: tomas

call-3.caption: We put mutual referral bonuses in their contracts. She hired someone against that income.
call-3.speaker: tomas

call-4.caption: Please separate the fake accounts from the promise we made her.
call-4.speaker: tomas

guide-segments.caption: Assign a policy to each segment. The forecast includes lost Guild revenue, not just saved rewards.
guide-segments.speaker: tomas

guide-grace.caption: Notice buys people time, but costs cash. Thirty days honors the month we promised.
guide-grace.speaker: tomas

human-1.caption: I called it a flywheel in the board deck. I should have looked past the curve.
human-1.speaker: dani

human-2.caption: Let's keep what works. I can live with a smaller number if it's real.
human-2.speaker: dani

guide-composer.caption: I'm Rhea, community lead. Give me a reason, timing, exceptions, and somewhere people can ask questions.
guide-composer.speaker: rhea

screenshot-1.caption: Someone posted our old message beside today's plan. Read both before you answer.
screenshot-1.speaker: rhea

revolt-1.caption: Reviews are falling. People feel the rules changed underneath them. We need to own that.
revolt-1.speaker: rhea

steady-1.caption: There's pushback, but people understand the change. Matching our words to the rollout helped.
steady-1.speaker: rhea

funding-1.caption: I'm Priya, your lead investor. We can bridge two million dollars for eight percent ownership.
funding-1.speaker: priya

funding-2.caption: That buys time. It doesn't fix the referral model. The dilution is permanent.
funding-2.speaker: omar

nofunding-1.caption: We have enough runway to avoid an emergency bridge. Keep measuring the customers we retained.
nofunding-1.speaker: omar

final-1.caption: We have one recovery team this week. Community support, partner repair, or a tighter cash forecast?
final-1.speaker: rhea

final-2.caption: Splitting it helps both teams a little. Pick what you can actually stand behind.
final-2.speaker: tomas

ledger-1.caption: Here's the ledger. What you kept, what you cut, and what it cost. Start with the conclusion.
ledger-1.speaker: omar

device-1.caption: One phone, fourteen accounts, no purchases. That's a fraud signal, not a neighborhood business.
device-1.speaker: omar

purchase-1.caption: The gold loops buy again without a bonus. That's the difference I missed.
purchase-1.speaker: dani

location-1.caption: Three neighborhoods. Different phones. These are businesses sending customers to each other.
location-1.speaker: tomas

no-pattern-1.caption: Account age alone doesn't separate these groups. We spent a check, but learned no useful pattern.
no-pattern-1.speaker: dani

report-ledger.caption: There it is. The stage left out circular rewards. The missing cost is two hundred ninety thousand.
report-ledger.speaker: omar

report-graph.caption: Some rings are huge. Others are just two shops. We can't call them all the same thing.
report-graph.speaker: dani

report-value.caption: Guild customers are worth four times the average. Cutting that loop would cut real value.
report-value.speaker: dani

report-device.caption: Fourteen accounts on one phone. Start there, before touching the shops buying every week.
report-device.speaker: omar

report-community.caption: People built routines around these rewards. They'll want a reason, not just a switch turning off.
report-community.speaker: rhea

report-contract.caption: That's our signature. Mutual referrals qualify. We need to handle this as a promise we made.
report-contract.speaker: tomas

report-cash.caption: Twelve weeks sounds comfortable until you need to raise money. The clock is already running.
report-cash.speaker: omar
